title: Assam, north Bengal districts on high alert; 12,000 evacuated from areas along Sankosh
where: Nation, page 11 (Sweety Kumari & Shinjini Ghosh); Odisha cyclone report (Sujit Bisoyi), same page
syllabus: GS1 › Important geophysical phenomena; Changes in glaciers · GS3 › Disaster and disaster management · GS2 › India and its neighbourhood (Bhutan)
summary: A glacial lake outburst in Bhutan's Gasa region put Assam and north Bengal on alert along the Sankosh, while cyclone Arnab's rains caused landslides and floods in Odisha.
ideas: Hazards cross borders: a glacial lake burst in Bhutan's Gasa region, sending water, mud and debris downstream into Indian river systems along the Sankosh.
GS1 · Geophysical phenomena / GS2 · Neighbourhood
Glacial lake outbursts in the Himalaya are transboundary hazards needing shared early warning.
Early action saved lives: about 12,000 people along the Sankosh in Alipurduar were moved to safety, with public announcements and disaster forces on standby; no major damage was reported.
GS3 · Disaster preparedness
Timely evacuation turns a hazard into a non-disaster.
Cyclone impacts reach far inland: under cyclone Arnab, torrential rain set off landslides in Odisha's Kandhamal and Ganjam, killing a family, and left about 300 villages marooned in Ganjam.
GS3 · Disaster management / GS1 · Cyclones
Cyclone risk is not only coastal: inland landslides and floods follow the rain.
Recovery needs administrators: Odisha deputed more than 30 senior OAS officers to Ganjam for relief and restoration of roads, power and health services.
GS3 · Disaster response / GS2 · Governance
Disaster recovery depends on surge administrative capacity on the ground.
Warming raises the risk: as Himalayan glaciers melt, glacial lakes grow, so monitoring them is now part of climate adaptation.
GS1 · Glaciers / GS3 · Climate
Shrinking glaciers and growing lakes make GLOF monitoring a climate-adaptation priority.
keywords: Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF)
Sudden release of water from a glacier-fed lake
GS1 · Geophysical phenomena
GLOFs are rising with Himalayan glacier melt and can strike far downstream.
Transboundary early warning
Sharing hazard data across national borders
GS2 · Neighbourhood / GS3 · DM
The Sankosh alert shows the need for transboundary early warning with Bhutan.
Cascading hazards
One hazard triggering others (cyclone → rain → landslide → flood)
GS3 · Disaster management
Cyclone Arnab's landslides show how disasters cascade.
Surge capacity
Extra staff and resources deployed in a crisis
GS3 · Disaster response
Deploying senior officers to Ganjam is surge capacity in action.
examples: About 12,000 people moved after a GLOF in Bhutan; no major disaster
The Sankosh evacuation shows how early warning and quick action prevent a transboundary flood disaster.
Landslides in Kandhamal; 300 villages marooned in Ganjam
GS3 · Disaster management / GS4 · Compassion in public service
Cyclone Arnab's inland landslides show that cyclone preparedness must extend to the hills.
pyqs: Melting Himalayan glaciers and India's water resources.
Shrinking Himalayan glaciers and climate change.
Disaster resilience and the Sendai Framework.
Infrastructure development vs disaster-risk reduction in ecologically sensitive areas.
potential: Glacial lake outburst floods are an emerging transboundary hazard in the Himalaya. Discuss the measures India should take, including cooperation with neighbours. (15 marks)

title: 'Godzilla' El Niño effects to be felt into 2027: decoding the WMO warning
syllabus: GS1 › Important geophysical phenomena; Climatology · GS3 › Food security; Disaster management
context: The World Meteorological Organization has warned that the intense 2026 El Niño will peak around year-end and affect weather well into 2027. It has already weakened India's southwest monsoon.
ideas: El Niño weakens the Indian monsoon, causing drought and heatwaves.
GS1 climatology · GS3 drought
El Niño weakens the Indian monsoon, bringing drought and heatwaves.
Effects into 2027 threaten food and water security and could push up fertiliser and fuel prices.
GS3 · Food security
The 2026 El Niño, lasting into 2027, threatens food and water security and could raise fertiliser and fuel prices.
keywords: Drought-proofing
Preparing farming and water systems to withstand dry years
Way forward
Drought-proofing farming and water systems is the answer to recurring El Niño years.
Food inflation
Rising food prices after a poor harvest
Climate and economy
A weak monsoon feeds food inflation, hurting the poor most.
Monsoon-dependent agriculture
Farming that relies on rain, not irrigation
Why India is vulnerable
Monsoon-dependent agriculture leaves India exposed to every El Niño.
Cascading risks
One shock triggering others: drought, prices, water
Systems thinking
El Niño brings cascading risks: drought, prices, water shortage.
data: Share of India's annual rain from the southwest monsoon
The southwest monsoon brings about 70% of India's annual rainfall.
India's 2026 monsoon, the fourth driest since 2001
India's 2026 monsoon ended at 87% of the long period average, the fourth driest since 2001.
pyqs: El Niño as a drought driver: the 2026 monsoon ended at 87% of LPA.
WMO warning: an El Niño strong enough to weaken the monsoon and affect weather into 2027.
Effects into 2027 on food and water security.
summary: The WMO warns that this year's intense El Niño, which already weakened India's monsoon, will affect weather well into 2027.
evolution: El Niño peaked at 2.3°C (NOAA data, cited in the report).
Current El Niño emerged and intensified rapidly.
Ended at 87% of LPA, the fourth driest since 2001.
